issues.description: Ingest clears warnings/stats but never clears results, so deleted or removed input rows remain stale in the database.
Ingest is not atomic across the full run; a parser crash can leave committed partial results with reset or missing stats.
Harness B assumes each JSONL value and metrics field are objects, so arrays, strings, numbers, or scalar metrics crash ingestion.
Malformed Harness C XML raises ParseError and aborts ingestion instead of recording a warning or skip.
Score parsing accepts non-finite floats such as NaN, which can violate database constraints or bypass range validation.
Harness A does not validate required run_id, model, or task fields before inserting normalized rows.
Harness B silently accepts missing IDs and inserts empty run_id rows, causing unrelated records to overwrite each other.
Harness C accepts empty run_id, model, and task values, allowing invalid canonical rows.
Harness A reads the CSV header but never validates it, so wrong column layouts are silently parsed positionally.
Missing or wrong input directories succeed as an empty ingest instead of failing fast.
Report opens a missing database by creating a new empty SQLite file, masking misconfigured database paths.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the requested target directory without safety checks.
The test configuration depends on pytest but the project does not declare any dev/test optional dependency.
Package version is duplicated outside pyproject.toml, creating an easy release metadata drift point.
Tests cover deterministic fixtures but miss malformed JSON/XML, missing identity fields, stale re-ingest behavior, and destructive fixture generation.
